newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle, pilots in new tentative pact.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle, pilots in new tentative pact.

text.p: Negotiators for AMR Corp.'s regional carrier, American Eagle, and its pilots union reached a second tentative labour contract less than two weeks after the earlier pact was rejected by the pilots, the union said Friday.

Terms of the pact were not disclosed. But the new deal addresses issues pilots had raised in rejecting the first agreement, such as better wage increases for first officers, guaranteed annual increases for pilots and improved scheduling, the union said.

The new pact also maintained some provisions from the previous agreement, such as offering a single contract for pilots at all four carriers that make up American Eagle and annual wage increases based on a formula tied to regional industry pay rates, it said.
The new pact is subject to approval by the pilot members, who will begin voting on August 12, the union said.
The Air Line Pilots Association and the airline reached the new tentative pact on Thursday.

"We think that negotiators addressed those issues that caused pilot concerns with the first agreement," said Capt. Homer Pugh, head of the pilots union's at American Eagle. AMR officials could not be reached for comment.

"We went back out to the line pilots to find out why that agreement was rejected. It's commendable that ALPA and company negotiators were then able to address and solve those problems so quickly, and I think that says a lot for our ability to work together," Pugh said.
If the new pact is approved, the contract will cover the four carriers that fly as American Eagle: Simmons Airlines, Flagship Airlines, Executive Airlines and Wings West.
American Eagle operates the world's largest regional airline system, with about 1,300 flights daily to 125 cities in the United States, Canada, the Bahamas, and the Caribbean.
